search.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Hexaploid tritordeum, the amphiploid <jats:italic>Hordeum chilense</jats:italic>×<jats:italic>Triticum turgidum</jats:italic>, has potential for bread making. In order to estimate the potential of bread wheat chromosome 1D for improving the bread‐making quality of tritordeum, and the processing properties and agronomic performance of euploid tritordeum, (1H<jats:sup>ch</jats:sup>)1D and (1A)1D substitution lines have been evaluated in field trials. No significant differences for agronomical traits were observed between the two substitution lines and the sister euploid tritordeum, except for the kernel weight of the (1H<jats:sup>ch</jats:sup>)1D tritordeum substitution, which was lower than that of euploid tritordeum. Gluten strength, estimated by alveograph deformation energy (W), and loaf volume were substantially higher in both substitution lines than in the euploid tritordeum.</jats:p>
title: Bread‐making quality in hexaploid tritordeum with substitutions involving chromosome 1D
